text:
Two goalies, 64 saves: Ottawa beat Calgary 2-1 in a game where both netminders were better than the shooters, and the Senators simply got their goals in before Devin Cooley locked in.

Ottawa owned the first period, 1.95 expected goals to 0.60, and cashed twice. Michael Amadio scored unassisted at 12:16, and Shane Pinto made it 2-0 at 17:37 off Stephen Halliday's feed. That was the end of the Senators' scoring. Cooley stopped Dylan Cozens on a 37% chance in the first and finished with 29 saves, 1.9 more than the shots deserved. Over the full game Ottawa produced 3.91 expected goals and deserved to win 71% of replays, so the margin should have been wider.

Calgary pushed back hard in the third, 1.35 expected goals to 0.66, and Matt Coronato finally beat Linus Ullmark on a power play at 15:40, his seventh shot of the night. Ullmark had the answer for everything else: 35 saves on 36 shots, 1.58 goals saved above expected, and the most wins added in the game. With talk in Ottawa about managing his workload, he made the case for playing him.

For the Senators, the questions are about scoring, not goaltending. Elliotte Friedman has linked them to Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, per Graeme Nichols, and two goals on nearly four expected is the kind of night that keeps that conversation going.

The Flames came in unsure of Martin Pospisil's status after the hit from Chicago's Wyatt Kaiser, who drew a three-game suspension. They lost but have little to be embarrassed about: Cooley gave them a chance, and Coronato's 21 minutes and seven shots were a reminder of who carries the offense when it works.
headline: Ullmark and Cooley trade saves, Senators hold on
